account: Wathour et al. (Ear and Hearing, published online 21 December 2022) ran a one-year randomized crossover trial. It had 24 newly implanted cochlear-implant patients at Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels. It compared manual fitting with the Fitting to Outcome eXpert (FOX). From 3 months the FOX group showed less variability and better speech intelligibility in quiet and noise. Median phoneme scores were 50%, 70% and 50% at 55, 70 and 85 dB SPL versus 45%, 50% and 40%. After crossover, 100% of the manual group kept the FOX map and 82% performed better with it. 63% of the FOX group preferred their manual map for comfort. A companion study (Otology & Neurotology, 18 January 2023) gave 47 experienced users a FOX map. It found median improvements of 10 dB at 6,000 Hz and 10% in phonemic discrimination and speech scores after 15 days of take-home use. Two 2019 case studies from the same group reported improved word recognition with AI suggestions in one of two adults. Otoconsult's site describes FOX as an outcome-based application assisting audiologists and AI-FOX as the successor of a deterministic first-generation tool. P. J. Govaerts co-authored all three papers. Whether any author is affiliated with Otoconsult could not be verified from the records read.

ai_role.statement: The software proposes MAP settings from measured outcomes. The trials compare it with manual fitting and attribute the measured gains to the FOX maps. All three papers share co-author P. J. Govaerts. The developer's identity is taken from Otoconsult's own site. No record independent of the authors' group is among the sources.

fields.account: Wathour et al. (Ear and Hearing, published online 21 December 2022) ran a one-year randomized crossover trial. It had 24 newly implanted cochlear-implant patients at Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels. It compared manual fitting with the Fitting to Outcome eXpert (FOX). From 3 months the FOX group showed less variability and better speech intelligibility in quiet and noise. Median phoneme scores were 50%, 70% and 50% at 55, 70 and 85 dB SPL versus 45%, 50% and 40%. After crossover, 100% of the manual group kept the FOX map and 82% performed better with it. 63% of the FOX group preferred their manual map for comfort. A companion study (Otology & Neurotology, 18 January 2023) gave 47 experienced users a FOX map. It found median improvements of 10 dB at 6,000 Hz and 10% in phonemic discrimination and speech scores after 15 days of take-home use. Two 2019 case studies from the same group reported improved word recognition with AI suggestions in one of two adults. Otoconsult's site describes FOX as an outcome-based application assisting audiologists and AI-FOX as the successor of a deterministic first-generation tool. P. J. Govaerts co-authored all three papers. Whether any author is affiliated with Otoconsult could not be verified from the records read.
